items.title: Revenue Grant: California Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) for the 2026-2027 “Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)” Grant
items.description: From: City Manager | Recommendation: Adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Manager or designee to accept the "Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)" grant and execute any resultant revenue agreements and amendments with the California Office of Traffic Safety. This OTS grant is $200,000 for the period of October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2027, which corresponds to Federal Fiscal Year 2027. | Financial Implications: See report
items.matchedInterest: Bike lanes, traffic safety and street design
items.plainSummary: Revenue Grant: California Office of Traffic Safety (OTS) for the 2026-2027 “Selective Traffic Enforcement Program (STEP)” Grant

items.title: Authorizing the City Manager to Submit a Local Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Cycle-13 Grant Application and to Execute Any Resultant Grant Agreement and Amendments
items.description: From: City Manager | Recommendation: Adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Manager to submit an application by November 2, 2026 to the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) for a Local Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Cycle-13 grant for safety improvements to thirty (30) signalized intersections along Shattuck Avenue, University Avenue, Bancroft Way, and Oxford Street; accept the funds; and execute any resultant agreements and amendments. | Financial Implications: See report
items.matchedInterest: Bike lanes, traffic safety and street design
items.plainSummary: Authorizing the City Manager to Submit a Local Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Cycle-13 Grant Application and to Execute Any Resultant Grant Agreement and Amendments

items.title: Enforceable Mechanism for Berkeley Green Code Compliance
items.description: From: Zero Waste Commission | Recommendation: Recommend Council to direct the City Manager to refer Public Works Zero Waste staff and Planning, Safety and Building, Energy and Sustainability and Green Building staff work together to develop recommendations to implement a clear path to enforcement for non-compliance with Berkeley Green Code (BMC 19.37) Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste diversion requirements, including the possibility of fines and citations and other mechanisms to increase compliance. | Financial Implications: See report
items.plainSummary: Enforceable Mechanism for Berkeley Green Code Compliance

items.title: Ashby BART East Lot Developer Selection for Exclusive Negotiation and Reservation of Predevelopment Funding
items.description: From: City Manager | Recommendation: Adopt two Resolutions that enable the City to move forward into negotiation and predevelopment with a selected development team for the Ashby East Lot Transit Oriented Development (TOD) project, located at the intersection of Woolsey St. and Tremont St., directly east of the Ed Roberts Campus, by: 1. Authorizing the City Manager or designee to negotiate and enter into an Exclusive Negotiating Rights Agreement (ENRA) and any required amendments with Satellite Affordable Housing Associates (SAHA), Habitat for Humanity East Bay/Silicon Valley, and Deborah D. Matthews Consulting (collectively, “the SAHA Team”). 2. Authorizing the City Manager or designee to negotiate and enter into an ENRA and any required amendments with the alternative developer, Related California and the Kelsey (collectively, “the Related Team”), in the event that the ENRA with the SAHA Team is terminated or if the City does not enter into a ENRA with the SAHA Team. 3. Approving the reservation of $1 million of Affordable Housing Mitigation Fees (Fund 120) to the SAHA Team or their affiliate(s) to support master planning and predevelopment activities related to the development of affordable housing at the Ashby East Lot BART site. 4. Affirming that the City's Housing Trust Fund Guidelines will apply to the use of funds to support master planning and predevelopment activities related to the development of affordable housing at the Ashby East Lot BART site. 5. Authorizing the City Manager or designee to execute all original or amended documents or agreements in accordance with the intent of this Resolution. | Financial Implications: See report
items.matchedInterest: Housing affordability and new apartments near UC Berkeley
items.plainSummary: Ashby BART East Lot Developer Selection for Exclusive Negotiation and Reservation of Predevelopment Funding

Informational Report On Citywide Staffing - September 2026
From: 		Human Resources Management Department
Recommendation: Receive An Informational Report On Citywide Staffing From The City Administrator Regarding (1) Citywide Vacancy Rates And Status As Of September 15, 2026, (2) Budgeted Vacancy Rate For Fiscal Year 2026/27 (3) The Vacancy Rates Of Regional Local Public Entities, (4) Recruitment Outreach And Community Engagement, And (5) The Analysis Of The City Workforce And Recruitment Conditions

items.title: BSCC Proposition 64 Cohort 4 Grant
items.description:
BSCC Proposition 64 Cohort 4 Grant
From: 		Economic And Workforce Development Department 
Recommendation: Adopt A Resolution Authorizing The City Administrator To: (1) Apply For, Accept, And Appropriate A Grant In An Amount Not To Exceed Four Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($4,500,000) In State Of California, Board Of State And Community Corrections (BSCC) Proposition 64 Public Health And Safety (Prop 64) Grant Program Funds; And (2) Expend And Administer The Prop 64 Grant By: (A) Assisting The City Of Oakland’s Capacity To Conduct Public Safety Operations And Coordinated Enforcement Of Illicit Cannabis Activities, Including Unlicensed Cultivation, Manufacturing, Distribution, And Retail; And (B) Enabling Equipment Purchases, Covering Overtime Staffing Costs, And Providing Funding For Other Related Administrative Costs Over A Five (5) Year Period Beginning July 1, 2026 And Ending June 30, 2031
